label: Weak, dense hum that rises on mental-health care vocabulary: words naming the field or its professions (psychiatrist, psychiatric, psychologist, psychology, 'mental health') and words for talking-cure care (therapy, talk therapy, counselling, sharing feelings in group sessions). Plain diagnoses (depression, anxiety) and therapy acronyms (CBT) stay low. Known side channel: the word ' talking' even outside care (a talking parrot ~0.3); ordinary medical scenes hum at 0.1-0.4, so it is a weak preference, not a clean switch.

label_history: ' talking' in 'talking therapy' within mental-health treatment text; the same topic without that phrase, and 'talking' in other senses, stay lower

' late' in the phrase 'too late' (a missed chance); plain temporal 'late', 'too early/soon' and 'never too late' stay near background. Separate second trigger: therapy/psychology vocabulary (not covered by this test)

Dense / gate-leak background unit: the - pole is a weak leak (max 1.52, 11% of tokens above 0.1 of max, 99.6% '-g +u leak') that hums at about 0.1-0.3 of max on most prose. Its feeders ('late' in any sense, lateness words, 'belated', 'little', ambient-it predicates) add only a small bump, so 'too late' / 'too little, too late' does not separate from matched text without lateness; the slightly stronger pockets are clinical-psychology / talking-therapy text (the + pole's topic leaking through) and the headline 'Too Little too Late?'.

Weak, dense hum that is somewhat stronger on clinical-psychology / talking-therapy text (psychotherapy, psychiatric symptoms, counselling sessions, psychodynamic or interpersonal treatment, ECT), the + pole's topic leaking through; lateness ('too late') adds little or nothing over matched text. Speech therapy also bumps it (solver).

Weak leak pole whose real driver is therapy / treatment text, strongest for mental-health treatment (talking therapy, counselling, psychotherapy, ECT, therapy groups at a clinic; speech therapy also counts). Lateness feeders ('late', 'too little, too late') add only a smaller second pocket in the fixed idiom; plain lateness does not fire it.

Weak, dense hum (gate-closed leak of the + pole) that is stronger on mental-health treatment by meaning, not by the word 'therapy': psychotherapy, psychiatry, counselling, ECT, psychiatric diagnosis (psychiatrist/psychologist sentences fire without 'therapy'; 'retail therapy' stays quiet; physical/speech therapy bump it partly). Narrow side branch: title-case ' Late' in 'Too ... Late' headlines ('Is It Too Late?' ~0.4, 'Too Little, Too Late' ~0.3), while lowercase 'too late' in prose stays at the hum (~0.14). The mapped feeders (L5/N4199+ 'too ADJ to', L0 故/遮 characters) do not lift ordinary too-late prose.

Weak, dense hum (11% of tokens above 0.1 of max) that is clearly stronger on clinical-psychology / psychiatric / talk-therapy text (psychotherapy, psychiatric symptoms, psychodynamic or interpersonal treatment, ECT, speech therapy); on top of that a smaller lexical bump on the words ' late' (strongest in 'too late', consistent with its 'too' and 'too ADJ to' feeders L0/N943+ and L5/N4199+) and ' talking'. Other feeder words (rain, ret-, bel-) do not carry through. Matched physical-medicine text stays near the base hum. This test checks the topic part only.

Weak, dense hum (11% of tokens reach 0.1 of a small max) that rises on talk-based mental-health treatment: counselling and therapy sessions, psychiatrists, psychoanalysis, psychodynamic work, where people talk through their problems; speech therapy and the word 'talking' bump it a little. Symptom lists and CBT jargon, where the + pole takes over, stay near zero. Physical medicine (surgery, physio, pharmacy) hums at the 0.1-0.2 baseline. Lateness adds nothing: 'too late' scores like 'too early', and the feeders' foreign too/late/tan words (demasiado, zu spät, поздно) do not carry through, apart from a small bump on the headline 'Too Little too Late?'.

Weak, dense hum (11% of tokens reach 0.1 of a small max) that rises on talk-based mental-health treatment and the writing around it: counselling, therapy sessions, psychiatrists, psychoanalysis, psychodynamic work, support groups where people talk through their problems (about 0.2-0.65); mental-health book outlines and speech therapy also lift it (inverse found 0.46-0.55). Physical medicine (surgery, dentistry, nursing, vets) hums at the 0.1-0.2 baseline. Lateness: plain 'too late' / 'ran late' stays near zero, BUT the feeders' late signal does carry through in the discovered-too-late construction ('noticed / realised / found out too late that ...', 0.2-0.45 peaking on ' late'), so 'lateness adds nothing' was too strong.

Weak, dense hum (11% of tokens reach 0.1 of a small max) that rises (about 0.3-0.55) on the vocabulary and settings of talking therapies: counsellor/counselling, therapist, psychiatrist, psychologist, psychoanalyst, psychodynamic/psychotherapy, group therapy, support groups, and also speech therapy (0.33-0.46). A crisis followed by 'weekly sessions' already lifts it before any profession is named. A plain paraphrase of talking about feelings with no care words stays near baseline (0.16), as do 'retail therapy', physical medicine (surgery, dentistry, nursing, vets) and cardiology (0.06-0.2). Lateness: lowercase 'found out / realised / discovered too late that ...' stays at baseline (0.08-0.17, not peaking on ' late'), so the earlier discovered-too-late clause did not replicate; only the capitalised headline 'Too Little too Late?' (0.35) carries a late signal. The spelling-piece feeders (ap/ag/pend/sp|ät) leave no lateness meaning here: German 'Verspätung' is near zero.

Weak, dense hum that rises on mental-health care and psychiatry in general, not only talking therapy: psychiatrist/psychologist, psychiatric hospital, antidepressant prescriptions, ECT, hallucinations / hearing voices, clinical, bipolar and postnatal depression (about 0.3-0.65). Physical-medicine twins (cardiology, burns, chemotherapy, fractures, infections) stay lower (0.1-0.3). Side channels: the '-therapist/therapy' word family lifts it even off-topic (physiotherapist 0.35, speech therapy 0.46), and the 'Too Little too Late?' headline; some disorder names alone (OCD, PTSD, anorexia, delusions) stay near the hum (0.13-0.22).

Weak, dense hum (about 0.1-0.3 on most text) that rises to about 0.35-0.7 on mental-health care and psychiatry as a topic (psychiatrist/psychologist, psychiatric ward, antidepressants, ECT, hearing voices, mania, psychodynamic), also in plain words (counsellor, mental health nurse). Physical-medicine twins with the same sentence shape (cardiology, burns, fractures, dialysis, antibiotics) stay at 0.05-0.25. A topic unit, not a word-form unit: psychodynamic 0.42 vs thermodynamic 0.08, and rare multi-piece words and split surnames stay at the hum, so the spelling-level traits of its mapped neighbours (surname tokens, 'George', -urge endings, multi-piece words, set-phrase completions) do not carry over. Side channels: the word 'talking' (from 'talking therapy'; 'the talking parrot' about 0.3), the -therapy family, and recovery/support-group framing (a knee-surgery support group reached 0.39).

Weak, dense hum that rises when text is about treating or caring for mental illness (psychiatric nurses and wards, antipsychotics, antidepressants, ECT, eating-disorder clinics, asylums, crisis teams), even without the words 'psychiatry' or 'therapy'; the same care scenes for physical illness (knees, measles, TB, cancer, diabetes, asthma) stay lower (~0.1-0.25), and mental distress told in plain words without any care setting (panic, grief, hopelessness) also stays near the hum (~0.15-0.2). Side channels from earlier tests still apply: the '-therapy' word family off-topic (speech therapy ~0.46) and the 'Too Little too Late?' headline. Its mapped neighbours (Texas names, shorthand text, re-typed strings) share no topic with it, so they do not change the label.

Weak, dense hum (the gate-closed leak of the strong psychiatric + pole) that rises when text is about treating or caring for mental illness: psychiatric wards and nurses, antipsychotics and antidepressants by name, ECT, eating-disorder and addiction clinics, asylums, community mental health teams. The same care scenes for physical illness stay lower (~0.1-0.25). Side channels that carry no mental-health meaning: the '-therapy' word family (speech therapy ~0.3-0.46) and the word ' talking' (from 'talking therapy': 'the talking parrot' ~0.29, found by the globalMOO inverse solver), plus the 'Too Little too Late?' headline. Its mapped neighbours (L23/N11310+, L6/N6776+, L24/N1091+, L1/N2546-, L26/N9961+, L0/N8268-) share no topic with it and do not change the label.

Weak, dense hum that rises on a word NAMING the mental-health field or its professions (psychiatrist, psychiatric, psychiatry, psychologist, psychology, psychoanalysis, 'mental health'), even with no treatment in the scene (a research psychologist studying memory ~0.5). Mental-health care described without such a word stays low (ward doses of clozapine and lithium ~0.14, the same as insulin; inpatient anorexia clinic ~0.12), as do psych- lookalikes ('psychic', the film 'Psycho'); the same sentence with 'doctor' instead of 'psychiatrist' drops from ~0.46 to ~0.14. Known side channels kept from the earlier label: the '-therapy' family (speech therapy ~0.46), ' talking' and the 'Too Little too Late?' headline. Of its newly mapped neighbours only L8/N2771+ (weight-loss surgery) is medical: after a gastric bypass, 'referred to a psychologist' ~0.65, 'referred to a surgeon' ~0.17.

Ordinary medical scenes without these words (dentist, nurse, ER) stay low.
